description: Bridge between algebra/trigonometry and calculus. Covers advanced function analysis, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic functions, sequences, series, and limits.

concepts.title: Piecewise and Step Functions
learning_objectives: Evaluate and graph piecewise-defined functions
Determine continuity at the boundary points of a piecewise function
Model real-world scenarios using piecewise functions (tax brackets, shipping rates)

concepts.title: Symmetry, End Behavior, and Leading-Term Analysis
learning_objectives: Determine whether a function is even, odd, or neither algebraically and graphically
Describe the end behavior of a polynomial function using leading-term analysis
Use arrow notation to express end behavior formally

concepts.title: Rates of Change and the Difference Quotient
learning_objectives: Calculate the average rate of change of a function over an interval
Compute and simplify the difference quotient [f(x+h) − f(x)] / h
Interpret the difference quotient as a precursor to the derivative

concepts.title: Combining Transformations and Building Functions
learning_objectives: Apply sequences of transformations to any parent function
Build complex functions from simpler ones using arithmetic and composition
Determine the domain of the resulting combined function

concepts.title: Graphs of Polynomial Functions
learning_objectives: Sketch the graph of a polynomial using zeros, multiplicity, and end behavior
Determine the maximum number of turning points from the degree
Identify the effect of multiplicity on the graph at each zero

concepts.title: Polynomial Division and the Remainder Theorem
learning_objectives: Divide polynomials using long division and synthetic division
Apply the Remainder Theorem to evaluate polynomials efficiently
Apply the Factor Theorem to determine whether a linear expression is a factor

concepts.title: Zeros of Polynomial Functions
learning_objectives: Apply the Rational Zero Theorem to list possible rational zeros
Use Descartes' Rule of Signs to predict the number of positive and negative real zeros
Find all zeros of a polynomial using a combination of theorems and synthetic division

concepts.title: Rational Functions and Asymptotes
learning_objectives: Identify vertical, horizontal, and oblique asymptotes of a rational function
Determine holes (removable discontinuities) in rational functions
Graph rational functions using intercepts, asymptotes, and sign analysis

concepts.title: Polynomial and Rational Inequalities
learning_objectives: Solve polynomial inequalities using sign charts and test points
Solve rational inequalities by finding critical values and testing intervals
Express solutions in interval notation and interpret them graphically

concepts.title: Exponential Functions and Their Graphs
learning_objectives: Graph exponential functions of the form f(x) = a·bˣ and identify key features
Distinguish between exponential growth and decay based on the base
Apply transformations to exponential parent functions

concepts.title: Logarithmic Functions and Their Graphs
learning_objectives: Define a logarithm as the inverse of an exponential function
Evaluate logarithms and convert between logarithmic and exponential forms
Graph logarithmic functions and identify domain, range, and asymptotes

concepts.title: Properties of Logarithms
learning_objectives: Apply the product, quotient, and power rules of logarithms
Expand and condense logarithmic expressions
Apply the change-of-base formula to evaluate logarithms with any base

concepts.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Equations
learning_objectives: Solve exponential equations by taking logarithms of both sides
Solve logarithmic equations by converting to exponential form
Check for and exclude extraneous solutions in logarithmic equations

concepts.title: Exponential Growth and Decay Models
learning_objectives: Model population growth, radioactive decay, and compound interest with exponential functions
Solve for time, rate, or initial amount in exponential models
Compare continuous growth (Pert) with discrete compounding models

concepts.title: Arithmetic Sequences and Series
learning_objectives: Identify an arithmetic sequence and find its common difference
Write the explicit and recursive formulas for an arithmetic sequence
Compute the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series

concepts.title: Geometric Sequences and Series
learning_objectives: Identify a geometric sequence and find its common ratio
Write explicit and recursive formulas for a geometric sequence
Compute finite geometric sums and determine convergence of infinite geometric series

concepts.title: The Binomial Theorem
learning_objectives: Compute binomial coefficients using factorials and Pascal's triangle
Expand (a + b)ⁿ using the Binomial Theorem
Find a specific term in a binomial expansion without full expansion

concepts.title: Parabolas
learning_objectives: Write the equation of a parabola with a vertical or horizontal axis of symmetry
Identify the vertex, focus, and directrix from the equation
Convert between standard and general forms of a parabola equation

concepts.title: Ellipses
learning_objectives: Write the standard form equation of an ellipse centered at the origin or (h, k)
Identify the center, vertices, co-vertices, and foci of an ellipse
Graph an ellipse and determine its eccentricity

concepts.title: Hyperbolas
learning_objectives: Write the standard form equation of a hyperbola centered at the origin or (h, k)
Identify the center, vertices, foci, and asymptotes of a hyperbola
Graph a hyperbola and distinguish it from an ellipse

concepts.title: General Conic Sections and Classification
learning_objectives: Classify a conic section from the general second-degree equation Ax² + Bxy + Cy² + Dx + Ey + F = 0
Complete the square to convert general form to standard form
Identify degenerate conics

concepts.title: Intuitive Understanding of Limits
learning_objectives: Estimate the limit of a function from a table of values and from a graph
Distinguish between the limit of a function at a point and the function's value at that point
Identify one-sided limits and determine when a two-sided limit does not exist

concepts.title: Computing Limits Algebraically
learning_objectives: Evaluate limits using direct substitution
Resolve 0/0 indeterminate forms by factoring, rationalizing, or simplifying
Apply the limit laws (sum, product, quotient, power) to evaluate limits

concepts.title: Limits at Infinity
learning_objectives: Evaluate limits of rational functions as x → ±∞ by comparing degrees
Determine horizontal asymptotes from limits at infinity
Evaluate limits at infinity for functions involving radicals

concepts.title: Continuity
learning_objectives: State the three conditions for continuity at a point
Determine intervals on which a function is continuous
Apply the Intermediate Value Theorem to show the existence of zeros

projects.title: Modeling Epidemics with Exponential and Logistic Growth
projects.description: Compare exponential and logistic models for the spread of an infectious disease. Fit both models to simulated data, analyze their predictions, and discuss when each model is appropriate.
learning_objectives: Build exponential and rational function models from data
Compare model predictions to identify strengths and limitations
Interpret horizontal asymptotes as carrying capacity in a logistic model

projects.title: Conic Sections in Orbital Mechanics
projects.description: Explore how the eccentricity of a conic section determines the shape of a planetary orbit. Plot elliptical and hyperbolic paths and relate their parameters to orbital energy.
learning_objectives: Classify orbits by eccentricity (circular, elliptical, parabolic, hyperbolic)
Relate geometric parameters of conics to physical properties of orbits
Graph conic sections with specified eccentricities and foci

projects.title: Infinite Series Paradoxes: Zeno to Fractals
projects.description: Investigate Zeno's paradox, the Koch snowflake, and Sierpinski triangle using geometric series. Prove convergence or divergence and compute exact values for perimeter and area.
learning_objectives: Apply infinite geometric series to classical paradoxes
Calculate perimeters and areas of fractal constructions at the nth iteration
Determine whether the infinite construction converges to a finite value
